episodes.title: How Elon Works
episodes.subject: Elon Musk
episodes.principle: Run Elon's algorithm on everything: question every requirement, delete relentlessly, then simplify, accelerate, and automate last.

episodes.title: How Jensen Works
episodes.subject: Jensen Huang
episodes.principle: War on complacency: keep the organization flat, criticize in public so everyone learns, and torture yourself and your team into greatness.
episodes.sourceBook: The Nvidia Way by Tae Kim

episodes.title: How Rockefeller Worked
episodes.subject: John D. Rockefeller
episodes.principle: Stack advantages into a flywheel: know your numbers, own your biggest cost, keep the deepest war chest, and turn competitors into partners.
episodes.sourceBook: John D.: The Founding Father of the Rockefellers by David Freeman Hawke

episodes.title: John D  Rockefeller: 38 Letters Rockefeller Wrote to His Son
episodes.subject: John D. Rockefeller
episodes.principle: Belief comes before ability: destiny is determined by your actions, not your origins — build what you're proud of and never make excuses.
episodes.sourceBook: The 38 Letters from J.D. Rockefeller to His Son by John D. Rockefeller

episodes.title: The Billionaire Who Automates Everything: Thomas Peterffy
episodes.subject: Thomas Peterffy
episodes.principle: Automate everything so the business runs on math, not intuition, and route around every arbitrary rule between you and growth.
episodes.sourceBook: Colossus Review profile of Thomas Peterffy by Dom Cook

episodes.title: How Bill Gates Works
episodes.subject: Bill Gates
episodes.principle: Build a business that fits your innate talents, then win through fanatical focus, ruthless cost control, and decades of endurance.
episodes.sourceBook: Source Code: My Beginnings by Bill Gates (with notes from Hard Drive, Overdrive, Idea Man, and In the Company of Giants)

episodes.title: Steve Jobs In His Own Words (Make Something Wonderful)
episodes.subject: Steve Jobs
episodes.principle: Life is short and the world is malleable, so impose rigor on yourself and make something wonderful that advances human progress.
episodes.sourceBook: Make Something Wonderful: Steve Jobs in His Own Words (The Steve Jobs Archive)

episodes.title: Peter Thiel on How to Build a Creative Monopoly
episodes.subject: Peter Thiel
episodes.principle: Go from zero to one by building a creative monopoly no one can copy, not by competing in an existing market; think for yourself.
episodes.sourceBook: Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future by Peter Thiel and Blake Masters

episodes.title: How Elon Thinks
episodes.subject: Elon Musk
episodes.principle: Reason from physics and first principles, not analogy; be useful, delete relentlessly, and endure the pain the mission demands.
episodes.sourceBook: The Book of Elon: Elon Musk's Most Useful Ideas in His Own Words by Eric Jorgenson

episodes.title: How Larry Ellison Thinks
episodes.subject: Larry Ellison
episodes.principle: You can't get rich doing what everyone else does: pick a contrarian bet, burn the boats, obsess over costs, and engineer every process.
episodes.sourceBook: Softwar: An Intimate Portrait of Larry Ellison and Oracle by Matthew Symonds

episodes.title: 400 Pages of Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger In Their Own Words
episodes.subject: Warren Buffett and Charlie Munger
episodes.principle: Think in opportunity costs, concentrate on a few wonderful businesses you understand, and let focus and compounding do the work.
episodes.sourceBook: Buffett and Munger Unscripted: Three Decades of Investment and Business Insights from the Berkshire Hathaway Shareholder Meetings by Alex Morris

episodes.title: How SpaceX Works
episodes.subject: SpaceX
episodes.principle: Atoms are cheap, process is pricey: redesign the whole stack around cost and validate it with fast, failure-driven iteration.
episodes.sourceBook: Atoms Are Cheap, Process Is Pricey — essay by Max Olson, from the forthcoming book SpaceX Foundation

episodes.title: Lessons from Jeff Bezos's Shareholder Letters
episodes.subject: Jeff Bezos
episodes.principle: Obsess over customers and think in decades; patient invention compounds into free cash flow and a franchise rivals cannot copy.
episodes.sourceBook: Jeff Bezos's Amazon shareholder letters (collected in Invent and Wander: The Collected Writings of Jeff Bezos)

episodes.title: The Stubborn Genius of James Dyson
episodes.subject: James Dyson
episodes.principle: Demand difference and retain total control, then out-persist everyone: determination, not cleverness, is what builds a real breakthrough.
episodes.sourceBook: Against the Odds and Invention: A Life of Learning Through Failure (James Dyson's two autobiographies)

episodes.title: Li Lu and Charlie Munger and Warren Buffett
episodes.subject: Li Lu
episodes.principle: Do one thing you love well, then concentrate: buy wonderful businesses cheaply and bet big on your few best ideas, the way Munger taught.
episodes.sourceBook: Li Lu's lectures, interviews, and writings (incl. his foreword to Poor Charlie's Almanack)

episodes.title: How Roger Federer Works.
episodes.subject: Roger Federer
episodes.principle: Play the long game: master your emotions, build a team you fully trust, and compound excellence over decades, not seasons.
episodes.sourceBook: The Master: The Long Run and the Beautiful Game of Roger Federer by Christopher Clarey

episodes.title: Napoleon (The Mind of Napoleon)
episodes.subject: Napoleon Bonaparte
episodes.principle: Fix your destiny, then bend the world to it with relentless action; plan timidly by imagining every danger, then act with total boldness.
episodes.sourceBook: The Mind of Napoleon: A Selection of His Written and Spoken Words (edited by J. Christopher Herold)

episodes.title: The Life of Jesus
episodes.subject: Jesus
episodes.principle: Lead an inward revolution of love and self-transformation, winning people through reason and example rather than spectacle or force.
episodes.sourceBook: Jesus: A Biography from a Believer (by Paul Johnson)

episodes.title: Rockefeller's Autobiography
episodes.subject: John D. Rockefeller
episodes.principle: Be brutally honest with your numbers, keep a fortress of cash, and compound first-class decisions with partners you keep for decades.
episodes.sourceBook: Random Reminiscences of Men and Events (by John D. Rockefeller)

episodes.title: How Steve Jobs Kept Things Simple
episodes.subject: Steve Jobs
episodes.principle: Wield simplicity as a weapon: blunt talk, small teams, one message per idea, and attack markets full of complex, second-rate products.
episodes.sourceBook: Insanely Simple: The Obsession That Drives Apple's Success (by Ken Segall)

episodes.title: Rick Rubin on Finding Your Life’s Work
episodes.subject: Rick Rubin
episodes.principle: Strip a work down until only its essential magic remains, then protect that fragile moment instead of thinking it to death.

episodes.title: The Man Behind Grand Theft Auto 6: Strauss Zelnick
episodes.subject: Strauss Zelnick
episodes.principle: Sustained success comes from being rational over decades and serving creative talent — hits are unexpected and can't be manufactured.

episodes.title: Marc Andreessen: The World Is More Malleable Than You Think
episodes.subject: Marc Andreessen
episodes.principle: The world is far more malleable than it looks — determined founders thinking from first principles can bend reality to their will.

episodes.title: James Dyson: 5,127 Prototypes
episodes.subject: James Dyson
episodes.principle: Progress comes from doggedness, not cleverness — treat failure as the most interesting teacher and iterate relentlessly until it works.

episodes.title: How Elon Thinks
episodes.subject: Eric Jorgenson
episodes.principle: Attack problems the future needs solved, reason from first principles, and treat time as the only true currency.
episodes.sourceBook: Scribe Media (author of The Book of Elon)

episodes.title: Jimmy Iovine: Building Interscope Records & Beats by Dre
episodes.subject: Jimmy Iovine
episodes.principle: Marketing is empathy at scale; win by attaching yourself to the very best people and telling them the brutal truth.

episodes.title: Jason Fried: Your Only Competition Is Your Costs
episodes.subject: Jason Fried
episodes.principle: Your only competition is your costs: keep them low enough that a few customers are enough, and stay independent.

episodes.title: Dana White: The Man Behind the UFC
episodes.subject: Dana White
episodes.principle: Own your content and its story, keep no Plan B, and let loyalty, not middlemen, build the empire.

episodes.title: Daniel Ek, Spotify | David Senra
episodes.subject: Daniel Ek
episodes.principle: Optimize for impact over happiness; happiness is a trailing indicator of impact, and greatness requires building a company true to yourself.

episodes.title: Ivanka Trump on Building an Authentic Life
episodes.subject: Ivanka Trump
episodes.principle: Know who you are before you build; a life and company authentic to you escapes competition and is the least replicable thing you can make.
episodes.sourceBook: Planet Harvest, Alexandria AI (formerly the Trump Organization)

episodes.title: Tobi Lütke: 21 Years of Building Shopify
episodes.subject: Tobi Lütke
episodes.principle: Don't cosplay orthodoxy — build from your own axioms and intuition; differentiation, not imitation, is the only path to excellence.

episodes.title: How Brad Jacobs Built 8 Billion-Dollar Companies
episodes.subject: Brad Jacobs
episodes.principle: Treat problems as opportunities, get the major trend right, hire people smarter than you, and repeat one disciplined playbook everywhere.
episodes.sourceBook: QXO, XPO, United Rentals, United Waste

episodes.title: The Marketing Genius of Steve Stoute
episodes.subject: Steve Stoute
episodes.principle: Run toward the unknown when it beats the known, and give creators ownership: if artists knew their fans, they wouldn't need a label.

episodes.title: Tony Xu of DoorDash: Surviving 1,000 Days of Startup Hell
episodes.subject: Tony Xu
episodes.principle: The data you can't see is what kills you: do the work yourself, run relentless experiments, and control what you can control.

episodes.title: Michael Dell, Dell Technologies | David Senra
episodes.subject: Michael Dell
episodes.principle: Take things apart until you understand them: curiosity finds the structural cost edge, and belief comes before ability.

episodes.title: Building Pixar, Working With Steve Jobs, and Cultivating Creativity | Ed Catmull
episodes.subject: Ed Catmull
episodes.principle: Put the problem, never who's right, at the center: candor works only when you strip authority from feedback and manage the room's dynamics.

episodes.title: CAA Co-founder Michael Ovitz: Failure Is Not an Option
episodes.subject: Michael Ovitz
episodes.principle: Your edge is frame of reference—a lifetime of meetings and outcomes; compound it with integrity, follow-up, and refusing to fail.

episodes.title: Evan Spiegel, Snapchat: Building a Multi-Billion Dollar Company
episodes.subject: Evan Spiegel
episodes.principle: No moat exists in software, so invest only in what is hard to copy—network effects, owned hardware, and a clear product vision.

episodes.title: How Todd Graves Built Raising Cane's
episodes.subject: Todd Graves
episodes.principle: Do one thing better than anyone and keep control of your baby; the distracted never beat the focused, and money follows service.

episodes.title: The Future of Software & AI | Cognition’s Scott Wu
episodes.subject: Scott Wu
episodes.principle: A startup has no right to win except by a concentrated first-principles bet on the future, run like hell—and a refusal to sell.

episodes.title: Bootstrapping a Business to $5 Billion in Free Cash Flow | AppLovin’s Adam Foroughi
episodes.subject: Adam Foroughi
episodes.principle: Ruthless efficiency—a few A-players plus a product that makes customers measurably richer—beats VC money, headcount, and a sales force.

episodes.title: My Conversation With Patrick O'Shaughnessy, Founder of Colossus & Positive Sum | David Senra
episodes.subject: Patrick O'Shaughnessy
episodes.principle: Betting on talented people before the world does is the highest-return act; grow without goals and run on clean fuel, not resentment.

episodes.title: John Mackey: 44 Years of Building Whole Foods
episodes.subject: John Mackey
episodes.principle: Build as a missionary, not a mercenary—never fight the low-cost rival on price, compound in your niche, and turn competitors into allies.

episodes.title: Brian Armstrong: When Washington Tried to Kill Coinbase
episodes.subject: Brian Armstrong
episodes.principle: A long-term mission simplifies the hardest calls—even suing your regulator—and a founder's edge is knowing he could rebuild from scratch.

episodes.title: From Near Death to a $20B NVIDIA Deal | Jonathan Ross, Groq
episodes.subject: Jonathan Ross
episodes.principle: Faster inference makes AI models smarter, and leaders move faster by declaring intent rather than asking opinions and inviting pessimism.

episodes.title: Roblox’s David Baszucki Built the Biggest Playground on Earth
episodes.subject: David Baszucki
episodes.principle: Build a perpetual motion machine: a closed-loop system where users become creators and an owned economy compounds virally for decades.

episodes.title: The Company Apple Couldn't Kill | Spotify Co-CEO Gustav Söderström
episodes.subject: Gustav Söderström
episodes.principle: Optimize for time well spent: prioritize the user over engagement metrics, and be great at the one thing that matters, average at the rest.

episodes.title: The $44 Billion Company Building Self-Driving Money | Eric Glyman, Ramp
episodes.subject: Eric Glyman
episodes.principle: Invert your industry: help customers spend less money and time, not more, and run every process through question, simplify, then automate.
